authority_order: playbook, normative schemas, source/platform contract locks

rule: An entry stays OPEN until the contract/addendum/schema is changed or the implementation is changed. While OPEN, the affected gate may not be claimed green and the implementation must take the SAFE side (the side that claims less).

entries.title: The U2S3 conformance lane has no profile in the normative catalogue schema
entries.contract: contract/typedb-r2-v14-upstream-test-catalog.schema.json — profiles[].profile_id is enum [U0,U1,U2,U3,U4]; contract/typedb-r2-v14-cargo-test-conformance-plan.md defines U2 as 'SlateDB LocalFS / file WAL / local'.
entries.implementation: The project executes a fourth conformance lane, U2S3 (SlateDB keyspaces over an S3-compatible object store, file WAL, local controller) and files its evidence under docs/evidence/G3/u2s3-full*. TYPEDB_STORAGE_PROFILE=U2S3 is a real, load-bearing runtime value (fork/typedb/storage/factory.rs).
entries.contradiction: The lane that carries the project's strongest structural-parity claim cannot be expressed as a required (leaf, profile) pair, because the contract's profile enum has no identifier for it. Its runs are therefore evidence about a profile the catalogue does not know exists, and completeness over the U2S3 lane is not derivable from the catalogue.
entries.safe_side_taken: required_pairs are emitted for U0..U4 only — the identifiers the contract actually defines. The U2S3 runs remain evidence LABELLED U2S3 (per the audit's instruction) and are compared structurally against the U1 oracle; no catalogue claims completeness for them.
entries.resolution_requires: An owner decision, then a coordinated change: add the profile id to the v14 schema enum and the conformance plan's profile table, or reclassify U2S3 as a parameterisation of U2 (object_store=s3-compatible) and say so in the plan. Do not add a profile id to the catalogue before the schema changes.
blocks: G1 completeness claim for the U2S3 lane

entries.title: The catalogue's zero-case declarations use the exclusion record, which the schema shapes for a different purpose
entries.contract: contract/typedb-r2-v14-upstream-test-catalog.schema.json — target objects are additionalProperties:false, so a target cannot carry a leaf_count or a zero-case reason; the exclusion record (subject_id/predicate/reason/owner/expiry) is the only declaration surface.
entries.implementation: 42 catalogue targets legitimately carry zero leaf cases (8 [[bench]] targets the cargo test lane compiles but never runs as tests, and crates with no #[test] functions). Before this session they were simply absent from every count, which makes an intentional zero indistinguishable from a lost suite.
entries.contradiction: Declaring them requires the exclusion record, whose fields (expiry, owner, replacement_test_id) are written for temporary carve-outs. A permanent structural fact is now carried in a record shaped for temporary debt, and it therefore acquires an expiry date it does not deserve.
entries.safe_side_taken: Declared as exclusions with explicit predicates ('cargo target kind == bench', 'libtest enumeration returns zero cases') and a far expiry, so the fact is visible and checkable today; validate_catalog.py cross-checks each declaration against the actual leaf count in both directions.
entries.resolution_requires: Either a schema addition (an optional target-level leaf_count/zero_case_reason) or an explicit statement in the conformance plan that structural zeroes are declared as exclusions and are exempt from expiry.

entries.title: The oracle baseline the U2S3 lane is compared against predates the package-id discovery fix
entries.contract: The conformance plan requires comparison against a U1 baseline joined by catalogue identity.
entries.implementation: docs/evidence/G3/u1-full/u0-results.json was produced before run_u0.py learned to parse cargo package ids, so every row records package '0.0.0'. The comparator therefore joins on TARGET NAME parsed out of the archived log filename, not on identity.
entries.contradiction: The strongest comparison in the project is joined on a weaker key than the catalogue provides, and two 0-case scaffolding targets share a name (handled as multisets). A name-joined comparison cannot distinguish two targets that differ only by package.
entries.safe_side_taken: The join is documented in the comparator and in every artefact it writes; profiles compare as multisets so a shared name cannot silently drop a row; the comparison now walks the union of both sides so a name present only in the oracle is a divergence.
entries.resolution_requires: Re-baseline U1 with the current runner (a full pristine-oracle corpus run), then join on cargo package/target identity. Until then the comparison is structurally sound but identity-weak, and it must not be described as identity-joined.
blocks: any claim that the U2S3 comparison is catalogue-identity-joined

entries.title: The upstream test catalogue is generated from a tree that the test lane cannot be running
entries.contract: The catalogue is the UPSTREAM denominator (docs/evidence/G1/upstream-test-catalog.json).
entries.implementation: libtest leaf discovery runs `cargo test --no-run` in sources/typedb and lists the compiled binaries. That checkout is either pristine (upstream, but then it is not the tree under test) or fork-staged (the tree under test, but then fork-owned tests inflate the upstream denominator). One warm build cannot be both.
entries.contradiction: Regenerating the catalogue and running the corpus require opposite states of the same checkout, so the two artefacts can never come from one build without a second checkout and a second ~9 GB target directory.
entries.safe_side_taken: The catalogue keeps being generated from the PRISTINE tree (upstream denominator preserved); the fork's additive tests appear only in run evidence, where the comparator classifies them per target with exact expected profiles. run_u0.py records the executed tree's own identity (checkout revision + staged-delta digest) so a result row names the bytes that produced it rather than borrowing the outer repo commit.
entries.resolution_requires: A second pinned checkout dedicated to catalogue generation (cheap in disk terms only where a second target dir fits), or a catalogue generator that enumerates leaves without a build.
